sections.h2: What is Tulsa like as a place to own and sell a house?
sections.html:
Tulsa is the second-largest city in Oklahoma, in the northeast corner of the state where the Great Plains meet the foot of the Ozarks. It covers about 183 square miles of land and was built on both sides of the Arkansas River.

The land is rolling, with hills such as Shadow Mountain and Turkey Mountain in the south, flatter ground in the center and north, and the Osage Hills reaching into the northwest. Downtown sits inside the inner dispersal loop formed by Interstate 244, Highway 64 and Highway 75. Midtown, with neighborhoods such as Maple Ridge, Cherry Street and Brookside, is the historic residential core. Much of the southern half of the city was built after 1970, West Tulsa lies across the river, and the north holds the airport and Mohawk Park (Wikipedia).

The housing stock reflects those layers: Craftsman, Tudor and Art Deco houses in the older core, ranch and Mid-Century Modern homes in south, east and Midtown, and newer subdivisions farther out.

sections.h2: Which county bills a Tulsa address?
sections.html:
Almost all of Tulsa is in Tulsa County, but small parts of the city extend into Osage and Wagoner counties, so the county on the tax bill depends on the parcel.

Wikipedia's school district notes say portions of Tulsa in Osage County are in Tulsa Public Schools, and portions in Wagoner County are served by Tulsa, Broken Arrow and Catoosa districts. If your house is near the edge of the city, look up the parcel on the Tulsa County Assessor's property search before assuming the county. For houses in Tulsa County, the Tulsa County Treasurer bills and collects the tax, and the Assessor sets the value.

Our Tulsa County property tax guide covers the county offices in more detail. This page stays on the city side: floods, utilities, schools, local liens and what they mean for a sale.

sections.h2: How does Tulsa's flood history affect a house sale?
sections.html:
Tulsa has a history of serious flooding and a nationally recognized response to it. A comprehensive flood management plan followed a 1984 flood that dropped about 15 inches of rain overnight, killed 14 people, injured 288 and destroyed 7,000 buildings.

In 2021 the City of Tulsa announced it had moved from Class 2 to Class 1 in FEMA's Community Rating System, the highest rank, with a 45% discount on National Flood Insurance Program premiums starting in April 2022. The city said it was one of only two communities nationwide at Class 1, and that the rating runs on a three-year cycle (City of Tulsa). Later city documents also describe Tulsa as a Class I community, but confirm the current class with the city before quoting a discount to a buyer.

  • Oklahoma's seller disclosure form asks about flood zone status, water seepage and drainage problems.
  • Gather any flood insurance declarations and elevation or repair records before listing.
  • If your house was ever flooded, tell the buyer in writing. Tulsa County's Assessor also asks owners to report damage from fire, flood or storm.

sections.h2: What does Tulsa's weather mean for roofs and heating?
sections.html:
Tulsa has a humid subtropical climate with just under 41 inches of rain a year, and its wettest month is May at about 5.9 inches. Severe thunderstorms with large hail, damaging winds and sometimes tornadoes are most common in spring and early summer.

Triple-digit days average about 11 a year, mostly from July to early September. Roofs and air conditioning units carry the heat and hail load. The Oklahoma Insurance Department notes that hail is the most common homeowners claim type, so ask your insurer about a separate wind or hail deductible before you decide on repairs.

Tulsa's economy grew from oil and has spread into aerospace, finance, energy and manufacturing. Wikipedia lists the American Airlines maintenance base at Tulsa International Airport as the city's largest employer, and lists Williams, ONEOK, ONE Gas and BOK Financial among headquarters in town.

American Airlines announced in February 2020 a $550 million, seven-year investment in the base. QuikTrip and several construction and engineering firms are also headquartered here. Wikipedia describes small businesses as more than 80% of the city's companies. Some of those figures are older, so treat them as background, not as current job counts.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Tulsa homes?
sections.html:
Tulsa Public Schools is the second-largest district in Oklahoma, with nine high schools and more than 41,000 students, according to Wikipedia.

It is not the only one. Parts of the city in Tulsa County fall in Berryhill, Bixby, Broken Arrow, Jenks, Owasso or Union districts. The district matters on your tax bill too, because rates are set by taxing district. The assessor's own worked example in its FAQ uses the Tulsa Public School District and a 2019 rate of $137.02 per $1,000 of assessed value.

sections.h2: How do I read a Tulsa property tax bill?
sections.html:
A Tulsa bill is built from three steps: taxable value, assessed value, then the rate for your taxing districts. The County Assessor publishes the formula and a calculator for it.

StepAssessor's worked example
Taxable Fair Cash Value$100,000
Multiply by 0.11 for Assessed Value (Gross)$11,000
Subtract the $1,000 homestead exemption$10,000
Multiply by rate per $1,000 (2019 Tulsa Public Schools example, $137.02)$1,370.20

That example uses a 2019 rate, so it shows the method and not what you owe now. The Treasurer's June tax distribution mailing shows how bills are divided among the schools, cities, the City-County Library, the City-County Health Department and the county (Treasurer calendar).

sections.h2: What city charges and liens can follow a Tulsa house?
sections.html:
City cleanup and mowing charges can become part of the property tax record. Tulsa County's tax auction notice says properties are sold for unpaid property taxes or for special assessments such as cleaning and mowing.

The City of Tulsa's nuisance abatement materials cover removal of tall grass, weeds and vegetation, and city records include resolutions authorizing the cleaning, cutting and mowing of property.

  • Drive by the property and look for notices on the door or the lot.
  • Ask the Treasurer's office at 918-596-5071 whether any special assessment sits on the parcel.
  • Pay or clear the charge at closing so it does not carry over to the buyer.

sections.h2: How do I transfer Tulsa water, sewer and trash service at closing?
sections.html:
The City of Tulsa turns on, transfers or shuts off water, sewer and refuse service through its utility office, and a change normally takes 3 business days after the request.

You can request it online, by email to Tulsa311@cityoftulsa.org, by calling 311 or (918) 596-2100 on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., or at Utilities Customer Service, City Hall, 175 E. 2nd Street. You must be listed on the account and have your customer ID and account number. For a shutoff, a forwarding address for the final bill is needed, and any balance is charged against your deposit first. Buyers of properties with a prior balance may need to appear in person with a deed (City of Tulsa).

Ask for your shutoff or transfer a few days ahead of the closing date.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work for a Tulsa owner with tax due?
sections.html:
A cash offer gives a Tulsa owner a way to sell without repairs, showings or a buyer's loan approval, and any property tax due is paid from the proceeds by the title company.

We look up the parcel, review the house, and give a written offer. If your tax is delinquent, we check the Treasurer's resale calendar so the closing date comes before any auction. We do not promise a price. You can compare the offer with listing and decide.

faqs.q: Who sends my Tulsa property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Tulsa County Treasurer, based on the value set by the Tulsa County Assessor. A few parcels at the edge of the city sit in Osage or Wagoner counties, which bill separately.

faqs.q: Is Tulsa in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Parts of it are. Tulsa has floodplain areas and a long flood history, and the city has earned the top rank in FEMA's Community Rating System. Check the specific parcel and ask your insurer.

faqs.q: How long does it take to move Tulsa utilities to a buyer?
faqs.a: The city says transfers and shutoffs normally take 3 business days after the request.

faqs.q: Can a city mowing charge affect my sale?
faqs.a: Yes. Special assessments such as cleaning and mowing can be collected through the county tax process and can lead to a tax auction if unpaid, so clear them before or at closing.

faqs.q: What is the 2019 Tulsa tax rate example in the assessor's FAQ?
faqs.a: It is a teaching example of $137.02 per $1,000 of assessed value for the Tulsa Public School District. It is not a current rate, so use the assessor's tax estimator for a current estimate.
